Postdoctoral research

Advisors: Elazer Edelman (MIT) and Farhad R. Nezami (Harvard Medical School)

AI and patient-specific modeling

Synthetic patient cohorts

A two-stage latent diffusion model that generates realistic 3D abdominal aortic aneurysms, ready for simulation. The synthetic shapes match the real patient distribution, so they can power virtual trials and train flow and wall-shear-stress surrogates when patient data are limited.

Automated image-to-simulation pipeline

A scripted pipeline that turns a segmented vessel into a finished simulation and its analysis with no manual steps. AI agents check each step, and physics-informed and graph neural network surrogates predict flow and wall shear stress in place of full runs.

  1. Prepare the surface and generate the volumetric mesh
  2. Assign outlet conditions: zero-pressure extensions, Murray's law or Windkessel models
  3. Run SimVascular or Ansys Fluent through its API
  4. Post-process flow, wall shear stress and vortices automatically

Left ventricular structure from CT

Quantitative geometry and texture of the left ventricle and myocardium. From a myocardium segmentation on CTA, I measure endocardial shape, extract radiomics texture features, and build ray-traced wall-thickness maps whose radiomics capture how uniform or heterogeneous the wall is.

Carotid geometry and calcification

An automated pipeline that segments the carotid arteries, extracts centerlines, splits branches and isolates the bifurcation. It reports diameters, areas, ICA-to-CCA ratios, bifurcation and planarity angles, curvature, torsion and tortuosity, and maps calcium by angle and radius around the vessel.

Virtual intervention

Virtual device deployment

Finite-element models of real devices, from CAD and mesh through crimping into the delivery sheath to deployment in the patient's own anatomy: stent-grafts for thoracic endovascular repair (TEVAR) of thoracic aortic aneurysms, and flow diverters for intracranial aneurysms.

Outcome prediction

AI-derived risk prediction for aortic disease

A proposed AI-derived approach to better manage aortic disease: combining patient anatomy with simulated hemodynamics to predict rupture or dissection, and links to hypertension and stroke.

AI-guided surgery

Patient-specific coronary bypass planning

Bypass surgery is still planned from visual stenosis grading, population guidelines and surgeon experience, with no measure of how each lesion limits flow or how a graft will compete with the native vessel. I built an AI-driven workflow that reconstructs the coronary tree from CT, chooses the best graft target and simulates blood flow before and after the bypass.

The full process takes under 10 minutes.

  1. Reconstruct lumen and calcification geometry from coronary CT
  2. Score candidate targets to find the best graft site
  3. Generate the virtual bypass graft
  4. Compare pressure and FFR before and after CABG

Angiography enhancement

AI-based enhancement with X-ray dose simulation that sharpens coronary angiograms, with vessel segmentation and stenosis quantification. Patent filed.

Future research program

Virtual intervention and cardiovascular digital twins, from the imaging suite to the operating room.

Angiography-to-VR surgical guidance

Advance my AI-driven CABG planning platform toward clinical validation, and extend the approach to EVAR for abdominal and thoracic aortic aneurysms, to intracranial aneurysms and to coarctation repair. The goal: from a 2D angiogram to a 3D patient model the surgeon can see in the operating room.

Cardiovascular digital twins

Surrogate models that predict post-stent vessel deformation and the resulting flow and wall stress in seconds instead of hours, so device choices can be tested on each patient before the procedure.

In-silico clinical trials

Synthetic patient cohorts with realistic anatomical and physiological variability, used to compare devices and surgical strategies across a whole virtual population before clinical studies.

Planned funding sources: NIH, NSF, American Heart Association, DARPA and industry partners.
